title: Talk an audience through a graph
objective: Name the axes, compare two values and state one message.

slides.title: Read the display aloud
body: The horizontal axis runs across the page. The vertical axis runs up the page.
Name what each axis measures. Include a unit when the values have one. Choose two values to compare.

slides.title: Model a comparison
body: Practice table: mean leaf length at week 1 was 2 cm. At week 2 it was 5 cm.
“The table shows mean leaf length in centimetres. It rose from 2 to 5 cm.”
Which words tell listeners the measure, unit and direction?

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: Across: time of day.
Up: number of birds.
Morning: 10 birds.
Evening: 15 birds.
Both counts took the same time.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Introduce both axes in your own words.
Compare the two counts. Give the change as a number and a percentage of the morning count.
Say what each axis shows.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: Across: time of day.
Up: number of bees.
Morning: 8 bees.
Evening: 12 bees.
Both counts took the same time.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Introduce both axes in your own words.
Compare the two counts. Give the change as a number and a percentage of the morning count.
Give a short spoken explanation with one clear final message.

slides.title: Give one clear takeaway
body: Ask your listener to sketch the direction of the change. Check the sketch against the values.
